title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #3

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these reduces friction? (1 mark)
   A. Rough paint
   B. Sand on a surface
   C. Gluing parts
   D. Ball bearings

2. Heat always moves from (1 mark)
   A. A dark place to a bright place
   B. A cooler place to a hotter place
   C. A hotter place to a cooler place
   D. A wet place to a dry place

3. Which is the best way of studying how a seedling grows? (1 mark)
   A. Pull it up daily
   B. Never water it
   C. Cover it in sand
   D. Measure its height every two days

4. What does the gullet do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes saliva
   B. Absorbs food into blood
   C. Stores faeces
   D. Pushes swallowed food to the stomach

5. Which of these is NOT alive? (1 mark)
   A. A young mango tree
   B. A plastic flower
   C. A grass blade
   D. A maize plant

6. Which of these is a healthy habit for digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Eating food that fell in dirt
   B. Washing hands before eating
   C. Drinking water from a dirty pond
   D. Never washing fruits

7. Which of these materials passes heat quickly? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Dry cloth
   C. Metal
   D. Wood

8. Which surface gives the least friction? (1 mark)
   A. Dry grass
   B. A thick carpet
   C. Rough sandpaper
   D. A wet, oiled tile

9. What does volume mean? (1 mark)
   A. How heavy it feels
   B. The colour of an object
   C. The amount of space an object takes up
   D. The amount of matter in an object

10. How many grams are in 1 kilogram? (1 mark)
   A. 100
   B. 1000
   C. 10
   D. 500

11. What do reflectors on a road or bicycle do? (1 mark)
   A. Make heat
   B. Make sound
   C. Make their own light all night
   D. Shine when car lights fall on them

12. Which of these is true of water? (1 mark)
   A. Plants do not need water
   B. Water is needed by all living things
   C. Only humans need water
   D. Animals do not need water

13. A school wastes 20 litres a day through leaks. How much in 5 days? (1 mark)
   A. 15 litres
   B. 25 litres
   C. 4 litres
   D. 100 litres

14. Which of these is a safe practice with light? (1 mark)
   A. Never look straight at the sun
   B. Look at the sun with your eyes
   C. Stare at bright lights
   D. Shine torches in eyes

15. What should you never do with oil that is on fire? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it with a lid
   B. Move away
   C. Pour water on it
   D. Call for help

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain why deworming is important and state two other ways of preventing worms. (4 marks)

17. Give three ways of saving water at home. (3 marks)

18. Explain why friction can be both useful and a problem. Give two examples of each. (4 marks)

19. State two jobs of the mouth in digestion. (2 marks)

20. Name the three states of matter and give one example of each. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Ball bearings
   Ball bearings roll and reduce friction.

2. C — A hotter place to a cooler place
   Heat moves from hot to cold.

3. D — Measure its height every two days
   Measuring height regularly shows growth over time.

4. D — Pushes swallowed food to the stomach
   The gullet squeezes food down.

5. B — A plastic flower
   A plastic flower is made by people and does not grow, respond or reproduce.

6. B — Washing hands before eating
   Clean hands prevent germs from entering the mouth.

7. C — Metal
   Metals pass heat easily.

8. D — A wet, oiled tile
   Oil and smoothness reduce friction.

9. C — The amount of space an object takes up
   Volume is the space a substance takes up.

10. B — 1000
   1 kg is 1000 g.

11. D — Shine when car lights fall on them
   Reflectors bounce light back.

12. B — Water is needed by all living things
   All living things need water.

13. D — 100 litres
   20 x 5 = 100 litres.

14. A — Never look straight at the sun
   Looking at the sun harms eyes.

15. C — Pour water on it
   Water on burning oil spreads the fire.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: Worms live in the intestines and take food and make us weak. Deworming kills them. Wear shoes, wash hands, keep nails short.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 1 mark each for other ways.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, use a cup or basin, fix leaks, use a bucket instead of a hose, reuse washing water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: Useful: brakes stop bicycles and shoes grip the ground. A problem: it wears out tyres and makes machines hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it helps in some cases and harms in others, and 1 mark for each correct example up to 3.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: Teeth cut and grind food. The tongue moves food and saliva wets it and starts digesting starch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct job.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: Solid (stone), liquid (water), gas (air).
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for the three states and 1 mark for correct examples.
